answer_1.quote: Our final benchmark tests whether large language models (LLMs) can infer emotion labels from narrative text via direct prompting.
answer_1.outputs: comma-separated list of single-word emotion labels

answer_2.quote: To evaluate the quality of these top-k predictions, we apply EMER-style set-based overlap metrics. Let Ŷ denote the set of predicted emotion labels for a given sentence and Y the set of gold labels aggregated across annotators. We compute set accuracy as Accuracyₛ = |  Ŷ ∩ Y | / | Ŷ |, [...] and set recall as Recallₛ = |  Ŷ ∩ Y | / | Y |.

answer_4.quote: To validate the reliability of our citizen science approach, we conducted an expert validation study using a random sample of 100 passages [...] independently annotated by the four trained moderators [...] We employed linear mixed-effects models to compare expert assessments with citizen scientist annotations across three emotional dimensions—valence, arousal, and dominance.
answer_4.guideline: comparison of annotations at dimensional (VAD) and categorical (NRC emotions) level using mapping pipelines
